title: Schema Management with apply_projection()
text: retrieve data CBN API, result contains every column endpoint offers — sometimes need, almost always names require explanation. apply_projection() lets take control raw data three things single, auditable step: Select — keep columns care . Rename — replace technical column names human-readable labels. Reorder — arrange columns sequence fits workflow. Every call silently recorded projection manifest attached result attribute. means can always look back see exactly done, done, — essential reproducible research.

title: Schema Management with apply_projection()
text: Output: data.frame class input, containing requested columns requested order, requested names — plus projection_manifest attribute.

title: Schema Management with apply_projection()
text: simplest use case: want two many columns inflation dataset. happened? Every column except date headline_yoy dropped. data otherwise unchanged — rows, values, order. keep columns, just extend vector:
code: library(opennaijR)  infl <- cbn("inflation")  # Keep only the date and headline year-on-year figure infl_basic <- apply_projection(   infl,   cols = c("date", "headline_yoy") )  head(infl_basic) infl_three_cols <- apply_projection(   infl,   cols = c("date", "headline_yoy", "food_yoy") )

title: Schema Management with apply_projection()
text: Renaming uses named character vector name left want column called, value right called now. rename subset columns, rest keep original names. Common mistake: Passing unnamed vector rename throw error.
code: # Rename all columns — no selection, every column is kept infl_renamed <- apply_projection(   infl,   rename = c(     Date     = "date",     Headline = "headline_yoy",     Food     = "food_yoy"   ) ) # This will fail — no names on the left-hand side apply_projection(infl, rename = c("headline_yoy")) #> Error: `rename` must be a named vector: c(new_name = 'old_name')

title: Schema Management with apply_projection()
text: can combine cols rename one call. columns listed cols dropped first, remaining columns renamed.
code: infl_clean <- apply_projection(   infl,   cols   = c("date", "headline_yoy", "food_yoy"),   rename = c(     Date     = "date",     Headline = "headline_yoy",     Food     = "food_yoy"   ) )  head(infl_clean) #>         Date Headline     Food #> 1 2010-01-01    11.80    14.60 #> 2 2010-02-01    14.05    17.02 #> ...

title: Schema Management with apply_projection()
text: Use order column sequence matters — example, dashboard expects specific layout, report important indicator appear first. renaming, use new names order, original ones:
code: # Put food before headline, even though we selected headline first infl_reordered <- apply_projection(   infl,   cols  = c("date", "headline_yoy", "food_yoy"),   order = c("food_yoy", "headline_yoy", "date") ) infl_report <- apply_projection(   infl,   cols   = c("date", "headline_yoy", "food_yoy"),   rename = c(Date = "date", Headline = "headline_yoy", Food = "food_yoy"),   order  = c("Date", "Headline", "Food") )

title: Schema Management with apply_projection()

title: Feature Engineering with derive_measure()
text: CBN dataset gives raw figures — year--year inflation rates, exchange rate quotes, money supply totals. derive_measure() lets turn raw figures analytically meaningful quantities: gaps, ratios, regime flags, rolling trends, anything else can express R expression. key design principle write formula directly inside function call, referencing column names bare variable names — $, [[]]. function evaluates expression dataset appends result new column. original columns always preserved. Every derived measure logged derive_manifest attribute reproducibility.

title: Feature Engineering with derive_measure()
text: Output: dataset one new column appended per expression. class existing columns untouched. derive_manifest attribute added (appended one already exists).

title: Feature Engineering with derive_measure()
text: common use: compute gap two indicators. new column gap_headline_food appears right data frame. Everything else unchanged.
code: library(opennaijR)  infl <- cbn("inflation")  # How far is headline above food inflation in each period? infl_gap <- derive_measure(   infl,   gap_headline_food = headline_yoy - food_yoy )  head(infl_gap[, c("date", "headline_yoy", "food_yoy", "gap_headline_food")])

title: Feature Engineering with derive_measure()
text: Note division zero: headline_yoy ever zero, ratio produce Inf NaN. derive_measure() automatically converts NA downstream analysis silently corrupted.
code: # What fraction of headline inflation is food-driven? infl_share <- derive_measure(   infl,   food_share_pct = (food_yoy / headline_yoy) * 100 )  # How does core compare to headline? infl_ratio <- derive_measure(   infl,   core_to_headline = core_ex_farm_yoy / headline_yoy )

title: Feature Engineering with derive_measure()
text: Use nested ifelse() build regime categories. Reading logic step step: headline_yoy < 0 → "Deflation" Else headline_yoy <= 5 → "Low" Else headline_yoy <= 15 → "Moderate" Else → "High" pattern scales many levels need.
code: infl_regime <- derive_measure(   infl,   inflation_class = ifelse(     headline_yoy < 0,  "Deflation",     ifelse(       headline_yoy <= 5,  "Low",       ifelse(         headline_yoy <= 15, "Moderate",         "High"       )     )   ),   reason = "Three-level inflation regime classification" )
